title: terraform: unify private state layout and migrate GPU node pools + IAM + networking modules
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: private deployments have accumulated multiple, inconsistent Terraform state layouts across GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking modules. This makes cross-environment upgrades and state migrations error-prone for customers running Redwood Private on GCP/AWS and for our on-prem installer. This PR unifies the state layout, adds migration helpers, and refactors GPU node pool/iam/networking modules to be idempotent and upgrade-friendly.

What changed: consolidated module state naming, introduced explicit workspace-safe resource references, added a state migration script (tfstate-migrate.sh) with dry-run mode, improved IAM role boundaries for node pools, and added networking validators for shared-vpc setups. Also includes a small README with upgrade steps and example Terraform workspace commands.

Migration plan and backwards compatibility: the PR ships a migration script that will create intermediate state mappings and preserve resource IDs. There is a documented rollback path that re-applies the old layout if validation fails. We did not change API surface of module inputs except where a clearer separate "instance_group" vs "node_pool" distinction helps avoid accidental resource replacement.

Testing and scope: tested against a GCP private deployment in CI integration (small cluster), manual AWS smoke tests, and an on-prem dry-run with the installer team. This touches private deployments only; hosted Redwood users are unaffected.

Checklist:
- [x] Refactor modules and update examples
- [x] Add state migration script with dry-run and verbose logging
- [x] Add unit-ish tests for module plan / diff using terraform-compliance harness
- [x] Update docs and upgrade README
- [x] Get infra & installer sign-off

Related Linear: ENG-4123 (state migration), INFRA-207 (private installer compatibility), PM-98 (upgrade UX)
commit_summary: Refactor: modules/gpu_node_pool -> split instance_group & node_pool resources
Feat: centralize state key naming and workspace-aware backend config
Chore: add tfstate-migrate.sh (dry-run + apply) and migration tests
Fix: tighten IAM role policies for GPU node pools to avoid overbroad permissions
Test: add integration harness for private deployments (small)
review_comments: Samir Gupta: Please verify that the state key rename will not force replacement for existing node pools. Can we add a mapping table in the migration script?
Maya Chen: Added explicit mapping table and a --dry-run flag. The script only moves state keys; it never recreates resources. Added plan outputs to the dry-run logs.
Ethan Brooks: IAM policy changes look good but please narrow the service account role scope for on-prem nodes. Left a suggestion in node_pool_roles.tf.
Maya Chen: Applied Ethan's suggestion and added a conditional to keep previous behavior for legacy_on_prem=true. Documented in examples/private/README.md.
Leo Zhang: Verified upgrade steps on a small GCP cluster and confirmed zero-downtime post-migration when following the README. Approving.
release_notes: Unify Terraform state layout for private deployments; add tfstate-migrate.sh with dry-run mode; refactor GPU node pool, IAM and networking modules to be workspace-safe and idempotent. See examples/private/upgrade-steps.md for migration instructions.
